title: Disentangled Sparse Representations for Concept-Separated Diffusion Unlearning
claim: The baseline unlearning method corrupts non-target concepts that share an attribute with the target; ours erases only the target and preserves the rest.
layout: 2 side-by-side image grids, rows are methods, columns are concepts, with red highlights
description: The figure shows a qualitative comparison grid of generated images, split into two halves by a vertical line. The left half is titled 'Erasing Dogs in Cartoon style' and the right half 'Erasing Frogs in Watercolor style'. Each half has three columns. The first column is the target combination, marked with a red 'no' symbol. The other two columns are non-target combinations that share either the object or the style with the target. Red text highlights the shared attribute. The three rows are Base Model, Vanilla SAE (SAeUron), and SAEParate (Ours). The base model produces clean images. The Vanilla SAE row shows noisy, corrupted non-target images. The SAEParate row has noise only in the target column and keeps clean dogs, flowers, frogs and rabbits in the non-target columns. The eye goes first to the colorful image grid and the red labels.
caption: Qualitative comparison of joint combination unlearning results. Unlearning results for the target style--object combinations Dogs in Cartoon style (left) and Frogs in Watercolor style (right). First column: target combinations to be removed. Other columns: non-target combinations sharing either the same object or style. SAEParate selectively erases the target while preserving non-target concepts, while SAeUron degrades non-target outputs due to latent space interference.
abstract: Unlearning specific concepts in text-to-image diffusion models has become increasingly important for preventing undesirable content generation. Among prior approaches, sparse autoencoder (SAE)-based methods have attracted attention due to their ability to suppress target concepts through lightweight manipulation of latent features, without modifying model parameters. However, SAEs trained primarily for sparse reconstruction do not explicitly enforce concept-wise separation, allowing semantically related concepts to share latent features. To address this, we propose SAEParate, which explicitly separates semantically overlapping concepts in the SAE latent space through concept-aware contrastive learning, supported by cross-attention-guided spatial aggregation that emphasizes concept-relevant regions. In addition, we enhance the encoder with a nonlinear transformation to increase its expressive capacity under this separation objective, enabling more concept-discriminative latent representations. Experiments on UnlearnCanvas demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, with particularly strong gains in joint style-object unlearning, a challenging setting where existing methods suffer from severe interference between target and non-target concepts.
